To make my life more interesting. 

These days, months, years, I have been reading many many manga. Seem every time I got bored at home, I would turn into manga. If I have finished old one, then I would keep on finding new one, until I found one interesting. 

From the beginning, **one piece, Naruto, Bleach, Touch, H2, History Strongest Disciple, Beelzebub, the world only god know, Gamaran, Minimum, Detective Conan, Yamada-kun to 7 Nin no Majo, Fairy Tail, Sankarea, Cage of Eden, Minamoto-kun Monogatari, Ippo, ...**

If I continue, it would be much more than that. But is it worth to spend wo much time in it? It seems that I found my life was boring, so I just keep seeking the life of others, the life in the virtual world. To get the excitement. To escape from where I belong. 

It has been my conclusion for a long time. I want to make my life more interesting instead. However, I would turn back to manga again and again. 

I know that if I do not focus on what I can do to make a difference, I would not be able to change my life to what I really want to be in my deepest heart. 

It was painful to get the pity from the others, even more painful not to able to help or protect the ones I love, make them worry. 

I really want to be stronger, to be the strongest. I determine to focus on it. To grasp every moment of my life again.

There are many different people in the world. They have different character, experience, and choice in their life. 

However, we share the same destiny in our life. We have limited time and would be old and death one day. 

When are not sure when would be our last day. What would happen in the next moment. That make life interesting. That should make us focus on the current moment. 

I don't really hate anyone because of what they do. They just make their own choice in their limit lifetime and want to choose their best solution. 

Anyone might be wrong, or do we have the standard correct one solution? 

In my life, I just want to get stronger and much stronger. 

To connect the dots: design the ways to learn or accumulated useful information or better ways of learning. Personally, corporately, academically, relationship.  

If we can keep on improving on something that really matter, then all of us, and our environment, shall be better and better. 

There must be ways to make our life much better. 

Technologically and human interaction. No matter what it is, I want to find the better solution. A better product. 

That's my goal.

never stop question myself
Is it the correct way?
I think that it depends\.

Sometimes it may not be right:
During the process if I have any doubt, then I would not be confident to act and achieve what I intend to do\.

And for some important point I should maintain my stance, other I won't have the base to proceed\.

However,
Shall I look back to review what is right or wrongly done?

I think I should otherwise, I would never be truly better\.

Chu Wun Yee,

You probably didn't know and I had never told anyone, I started love you when there was once I chased a ship and carelessly bumped into a bench.  I blocked with my palm and half of it turned bruised the following day when I came to school. 

I couldn't remember what you did when you saw my injury, but you looked worry. Then I fell in love. 

At that time, I found that I didn't have the courage to talk to you, even if I was seated next to you. I didn't think that I was good enough to deserve what I wanted. And afraid of losing something by taking any stupid action.

I just kept looking at you from behind as if there could be any change by just looking. It just made others aware of it and caused you a lot of trouble. I am sorry about that. 

You later rejected me politely even I have never confessed. 

It has been about 17 years since we knew each other. I never regret ever love you. But I know that not taking any action was the stupidest thing I ever did. 

I wish I could have talked more with you and understood more about you. So that we could know better if we suit each other. 

Not sure if I could have that chance again. If I do, I wish to ask you out once in a while. Or start with going to work together. 

Perhaps you are currently in relationship with other then I would be very happy for you!  Or you have other reasons, then you could reject me again this time. I promise, I will never ask you again. 

Either way, I would be grateful to have your answer. 

Cheers,
Cheung Chun Ping

End of first love
So my first love properly ended after my confession.
I have to move on and start stronger.

It takes 17 years and now it is the end.

I actually feel relaxed. As I can properly move on.

When I looked back, it seems that what I feared most later was what if I succeed. I actually not that much want to be in relationship with her. I just want to end it and then move forward.

Could I be blamed? Of course! I'm a man, I should properly face my feeling and confront what I what stand in front of me.

That would have cause much less trouble and waste much less time on meaningless things.

There are something that can't be known by just thinking.

Is it what you want? I have to determine it by facing it.

I may not be able to see her again. But I'm thankful for it finally ended.

Stupid things I did
There are actually many stupid I did in my life. 

If I really want to be a better man, I have to control myself

What is stupid? To want to get the things in a wrong way, which I won't get it in such a way
E.g. In my birthday last year, I walked lonely on the bridge, then there is a guy from California fitness invited me to have a look on their fitness center. 

Since it was the 2nd time he asked me, I thought just take a walk is fine. So I enter. 

I didn't aware that it was one of the costliest decision I ever made which have zero value to me. Or even negative value. 

A woman brought me along to introduce the center and then she was supposed me that I would join them, but in reality I never had such intention. 

Firstly, a guy as me to join the membership. 
It is a few hundred a month. For 5 years. 

Well I actually don have the interests to going to the gym room.  I just want to be free and don't want to limited by time and location to do exercise. It was just not my type to do any exercise in gym room. 

The only reason I could think of was to build up my core muscle to run faster and more durable. 

But still there are just so many other better way that's suitable to me.

I am okay with every thing. So I just accepted that. And signed the contract and pay the pre- installment. 

Then they ask me to do muscle building. 

Well, I just want to train myself. No need for anyone bothering me. 

But then I was persuaded. 

If I don't really decide myself, all my life would just be random decision made my the other. And that would never be my life. 

I have to cut my low lever decision out of 
- stupid fear, cowardice, lust, food, money

What I really want in my deepest heart I had always know and it would never be gotten in a wrong way.

從難於易
我們做事從來都只能從難於易，並不是指面對困難要於棄。
而是要將一件困難的事按步就班一步步做好。看似自相矛盾，其實不然。
面對一件困難的事情的時候，它之所以困難是因為在當時有所不足，
－ 沒有足夠的能力
－ 時機未到
－ 很到其他的時情並末能配合

在這個時候，根本沒有可能一蹴而就。但如果某件事情是無論如何都希望要做到的話便要找尋可前進的道路，可解決的方法。
它的易，是因為在當時我是力所能及；但亦不可以說它不難。因為越值得我們做的事情往經過很多失敗的嘗試，或需要不斷可能有些枯燥的鍛練。在這時，它的難，不是事情的本身，而是能否堅定不移地前進。

但在日常生活中，實在有太多容易事情我們可以做到。而這些事情往往立刻便能令你「快樂」。電視，漫畫，電影，小說，這些東西並不一定是壞，可是由於得之太易，往往會浪費了很多時間在這些事上而不能專注於真正重要的，看似枯燥的事情上。

可口的東西吃多了往往對身體有害，要有所調節。
能夠在平凡中見到真趣，才能得到真正的快樂。

Find a way to keep track in my knowledge, so that for whatever aspect of my life, I can access it quickly and easily.

No matter it is writing or thinking or drawing. 

Probably that about if I have to present the material, what I would do?  How I would organize it to make it easier for people to understand.

Meanwhile, I would have more things to present in my daily life and in achiever meeting. 

It kill two birds with one stone.

Lots of ideas I have known, but it just needs me open my mind to try it. Nothing to lose even if I fail.

And then relax in the way of playing taichi or yoga. The mind could be relax as well.

禍從口入
　　中醫師經常提醒患有皮膚病病人戒口，這是因為很多食物都是皮膚病的致敏源頭，只要我們遠離致敏食物，就能有效防止癮疹的出現。

一般皮膚病患者需要戒口的食物有：
1. 水果類：菠蘿、荔枝、芒果、榴槤、龍眼、大樹菠蘿等。
2. 海鮮類：幾乎所有的海產類食品都要戒除，如蝦、蟹、蜆、螺、蠔、青口、帶子、魷魚、無鱗魚等，傳統中醫都稱之為「腥臊發物」；如患者進食有鱗魚類後出現皮膚過敏，亦需戒掉。
3. 肉類：中醫認為鵝肉、牛肉是熱毒的食物。
4. 蔬菜類：菇類、竹筍、辣白菜等。
5. 烹調方法：忌用辣椒、咖喱等辛溫類的調味料煮菜，避免油炸、燒烤。
6. 飲料：酒、咖啡、豬骨湯、參茸進補湯等。
7. 藥物：許多藥物通過引起機體變態反應而導致蕁麻疹，例如亞士匹靈、青黴素等。

除了戒口以外，還需注意︰
1. 避免接觸致敏的物質如花粉、動物皮毛、護膚品等。
2. 注意氣溫變化，自我調攝寒溫。雖然夏天氣候炎熱，但亦應隨身帶一件外套，當進入冷氣地方時，皮毛容易受寒吹風，不要等到起雞皮疙瘩才保暖。
3. 加強身體鍛鍊，適量的運動可促進氣血運行，身體健康，才能抵禦風寒侵襲。
4. 避免長時間日光照射
5. 恆常保持心境開朗，使情志舒暢，肝氣順達。

備註：以上資料僅供參考，如有任何疑問請向註冊中醫師查詢。

Morning Pages - 3 pages a day
It is not supposed to be something smart or any thing. Just write anything in my mind. For 3 pages. It is something that I never imagine. 

I think this kind of practice can not only do in writing, but also in many other aspects:
- Martial art
- Drawing
- Coding
- Work

Just keep on doing, no matter how pointless it is. It is a process of discovery. Something happen so much everyday, I have to give it a digestion anyway. To writing as fast as possible. So that there is no gap for thinking. It is the way to free up anything hidden in my mind. The potential that I have.

This topic of learning haVe been in my study and practice for very long time. I have always been wishing to get some breakthrough.

Perhaps, I shall also do it in my public speaking and making girl friends....

The words in my mind might not be release if I don’t use it.
It is just a knowledge before I can use it and become and become part of myself.

NO MATTER How busy I would be, I think keep on writing is okay to me. AS I have time in transmute, that time is enough for writing 3 whole pages. How could I write faster so that I won’t need to have time of thinking. I think I can improve the tools and practice my skills. 

The tools of using iPhone to write might be a bit slow, perhaps I shall consider to write before having my breakfast in my home. That way I can best use of my time??? 

But any way, I have to take the time for think of reading. Which time is best to doing which it is determine by the efficiency and effectiveness. 

I think my writing in recent shall cover the following areas as well:
- QP final exam
- Work
- Home building
- Art

Never give up, as this is the area that I have to improve. Perhaps I shall also learn Chinese typing so that I can improve my communicate with Chinese as well. It is the areas that I haven’t been developed for a long time. But I actually quite like Chinese language, wisdom and culture. Although there’re many Hongkonger don’t like about it.

Wherever, whatever, I think I can ‘t stop here. Because nothing good would be come out just by waiting. I think it is not just writing. IN the process of writing, I shall keep thinking about how to make it better next time. Just like live everything day, if I never think about how to improve the days, I would just repeat doing the same thing but not progress. What I really want is to be a better man, it has been mentioned by me many many times. 

Don’t need to be in the mood of writing. Just write. No matter how bad or how good it is.
Because day by day, with more study and trial and error, I would find the way to lead to a better self. But if I  just read but not write, if I just learn but not do, then it is pointless, as I would forget it quickly. Just like what I learnt in mechanical engineering. All of them is just like a long history. What remains are books on my bookshelf. I don’t want to waste my time. I want to treasure every moment. So grasp it by writing and learning and make it a spiral process. It just takes me little time, but the impact, i believe, would be significant. 

I have no more regret in what I have done. As what is past is past. But I decide to do whatever I can to keep my promise and proceeding to be a man I am proud of..

忘了
太多事我認為重要， 但隨着時間的流逝我卻會忘了。
我可以控制自己的大腦而不是被它控制。

当我们决心改变的时候，“懒惰”便会指使我们的那个“大脑的自我保护功能”——“遗忘”——起作用，让我们不知不觉停止改变。

好记性不如烂笔头

我以往一段時間做過什麽呢？
昨天：跟Kammy 行山，到了蚺蛇尖，有不少地方是比平時行的路段崎嶇的。天陰，但清涼。因有些累，8時才起床，9時出門，10時前到了西頁碼頭，跟她會合然後乘94號到北潭凹。

前天上班主要是做month-end。

上一個月呢？完成了OTT HK的audit.
.....

如果你想改变你自己，或者你目前的处境并不令人满意，那就一切从简——找一个你觉得该给你带来改变的行动，然后去做就是了。不要怕碰壁，不要怕失败，那是必须经历的一个过程。还是那句话，失败并不可怕，因为你总是要失败许多次才会有结果，并且又不是全天下只有你一个人失败，怕什么？关键在于在每次挫折之后能否吸取教训。只要能吸取教训，然后自我调整，那就是进步了。

# We are what we repeatedly do, excellence then is not an act but a habit \- Aristocles

Have just read a bot about habit\.
It reminded of a few key things\.

1. How habit work Habit is not about memory, it is control by any other part of the brain, so that we could do things automatically\. It is an mechanism to help people to react immediate, with less demand on willpower\. It is especially important when we are under stress\.

That’s why we shall build a good habit\.

Even if it’s a minor habit, it would be like a rolling snowball that become big\.
To me, it shall be writing journal\.

Cue routine reward \- craving the endorphins or sense of accomplishment
Belief \- people might be skeptical about their ability to change if they’re by themselves, but a group will convince them to suspend disbelief\. A community creates belief\.”

When things got really tense, they went back to their comfort zones

Small win \- once a small win has been accomplished, forces are set in motion that favor another small win

Signing kids up for piano lessons or sports is so important\. it has nothing to do with creating a good musician or a five\-year\-old soccer start, when you learn to force yourself to practice for an hour or run fifteen laps, you start building self\-regulatory strength\.

1. Keep track
2. Make a plan ahead and practice

If people are asked to do something that takes self\-control, if they think they are doing it for personal reasons \- if they feel like it’s a choice or something they enjoy because it helps someone else \- it’s much less taxing

If they feel like they have no autonomy, if they’re just following orders, their willpower muscles get tired much faster\.

What about my work? My study? My health? My relationship?

Hiking - Ching Shan
It was the first time I went to this mountain. Originally, thought, it was a well-developed place, not much surprise. And at the beginning, only saw temples and asphalt roads. After 15 min walk, we got closer to the slope.

I went ahead first to reach the peak to see how it look like there.

![](dayone-moment://5D16B05E70124BE899DB6ECA22E38E93)

it was beautiful. Saw many mountains at the top. I was a bit hungry, but we still continue to walk, we want to find another way to leave. They way we used is similar to what I found from the web http://www.walkonhill.com/route.php?area=4&seq=6

After I reached the peak, I came back and saw her struggling to climbing up.
Well, in fact, all the way to the peak was climbing stairs. 550m. It wasn’t easy for one who didn’t walk much. It was how she look like when she arrived the peak.

When she was taking rest, I walked around and discovered the other ways to left. So I got back took some photos and grabed her. The other way turn out to be playful, interesting to hike. It is a bit challenging for some people, but overall is save, as there were not much sharp cliff. 

We continue to walk for another 3 hours. leaving around 2 pm.

Had lunch at Saizeriya Italian Restaurant in a shopping mall of Yeun Long and then took bus to Tsuen Wan and then back home with 290.

GST, Singapore Tax
levied on the import of goods (collected by Singapore Customs), as well as nearly all supplies of goods and services in Singapore.

![](dayone-moment://E1CA7E17F3974F329E53F541C4F507B2)

GST is a tax on **local consumption**, i.e. it is levied on all services consumed in Singapore whether they are procured from local or overseas suppliers. Based on current GST rules, services (other than an exempt supply) supplied by a supplier who belongs in Singapore is subject to GST while the same services supplied by a supplier who belongs outside Singapore is not.

To level the GST treatment for all services consumed in Singapore, the Minister for Finance announced in Budget 2018 that the following regimes will be implemented from 1 Jan 2020 to tax imported services:

Reverse charge regime for Business-to-Business (“B2B”) supplies* of imported services; and
Overseas vendor registration regime for Business-to-Consumer (“B2C”) supplies* of imported digital services.

# Finance

For a company, it could get the **source of finance** from the following:

![](dayone-moment://A944662283804B78B4DA12DDFB2978B9)

**Equity**

- Owner equity
- Partners \- normal, 
- Investors
- Public
- Earnings of the company

**Debt**

- Bank loan long term, short term
- Account payables 

What are the effect to a company?
Dr cash, Cr\. Equity
Dr cash, Cr\. Liability

Asset = Liability \+ Owners equity
Risk is higher for equity owners\. 

Funding has cost \- cost of capital
Capital structure

**Liquidity vs profitability**
Company need funding to expand quickly
However, expansion often mean losing money\. 

**Presentation to external** 

- Owner interest in profitability, 
- Lender, supplier interest in debt level and liquidity
- Customer interest in 
- Government interest in tax
- Employer / employee

Framework \- HKAS, HKFRS

AGM to present the results
**Agency problem \-\-> control**

- Internal control \- Internal audit
- External Audit

Conflict of interest
Code of Ethic

Listing company \- code

Business and tax

slept late because of work\. Arrived home around 12pm\.
in to plane, I was drawing a summary about what I learnt for the QP subjects

That’s why I have to have a clear outline first\. From there, I can start study everyday without losing track of what I’m studying\.

Not watched movie\.

after landing, i was tired, taking brother private car to his house\. Not much change in his house\. I wanted to work on MOOV red label calculation\. But was too tired to accomplished it\. 

SO I will do it tomorrow morning\. At such time, I shall be able to get rid of the jet lag\.

I want to buy a bicycle\. SO that I can travel freely in the city\. 
Perhaps, it could be stored in the back truck of the car\.

but before that I shall finish the task related to MOOV\.
And later tomorrow, shall assign the work to Katie day by day\.

# It would be my last day of the long holiday\. 

![](dayone-moment://C50619EDB1DF403FB7BB02BFCD899226)

After the flight to HK\. It would be the end of the holiday\. Then I shall start another moment of life\. 

Think a lot about the things could be improved during the holiday\. And also did something for the work, e\.g\. organizing the mail box, got back to some email related to work\. 

With great discovery was that I could use vpn\. Then going forward, much could be done  outside office\. 

The implication is that the thailand and Singapore colleague could extract data themselves from oracle\. \- 

- [ ] I shall arrange that from monday\. 

Besides, have read a book about drawing ideas\. That’s a good one\. I learnt what is the actual seeing\. In the past I just got short or instant memory to draw a picture, but that won’t help much for my skills\. 

Same go to my study and work and other aspects of my life\. 

While I spent more time with my mother, I found there are needs to improve her life with something\. 

- [ ] Green tea
- [ ] Stair for exercise
- [ ] Apple Watch and iPhone
- [ ] Remodeling of the apartment
- [ ] Cup or utensils to keep things warm
- [ ] Company
- [ ] Better quality foods

For my study, I already have a outline\. From now on I would study the subject everyday\. Whenever I have the time\.\.\. slot it\. 

I become more skillful in riding bicycle\. It wasn’t intended\. But anyway, I rode on the road\. 

With better organized, I shall have more personal time and pass the coming exam\. 

Besides, I shall take more time with my mother, or organize better so that we won’t get bored during the day\. 

After the trip, it would be the mid\-autumn festival\. Will take mom to eldest brother home\. And bring along the souvenirs\. 

As long as I organize the knowledge I have better, it doesn’t matter when and where I input the info\. Even if it is discrete\. 

Because I can connect it\. 

It would be tired to keep on doing the same task for a long period\. And it is inefficient\. 

Other than personal,

entries.text:
# Due diligence

![](dayone-moment://B1BA50C93FA14FA39F49A7C7FCE032CF)

Investigation into a potential investment \- usually carried by a professional firm on behalf of investors\.

- Involves an examination of operations and management and the verification of material facts
- Areas to cover: commercial, financial, legal, other

Commercial

- top down analysis
- Understanding the stage of the organization in its life cycle
- The link with strategy
- Strategic analysis, including SWOT and Porter’s five forces
- The changing environment: environmental, social and political risks

Financial due diligence

- The statement of financial position
- Contingencies, capital commitments, leases, etc\.
- Intangibles – measuring and managing IP, brands, goodwill, etc\.
- Forecasts – identifying variables most at risk

Legal due diligence

- Getting the corporate legal structure right
- Understanding legal documents, such as Sale & Purchase agreements
- The legal environment: Takeovers Code, Employment Law, etc\.
- Tax implications: Capital gains, assessed losses, etc\.

Other areas: Corporate culture, IT, Intellectual Property and Environmental due diligence

- Understanding the people perspective
- Identifying environmental risks
- Quantifying the costs of meeting any continuing and/or future obligations\.

#QPB

- The SFO Share Buy\-Backs Code \(covered in Chapter 18\) #QPB

entries.text:
# Accountant’s report and pro forma financial information

![](dayone-moment://0C5769F6B5C14198B0C941EAD0183CB5)

Chapter 4 of the Main Board Listing Rules sets out the detailed requirements for accountants' reports on the profits and losses, assets and liabilities of, and other financial information on, an issuer of securities\. These requirements include the following:

\(a\) All accountants' reports must be prepared by certified public accountants, who are qualified under the Professional Accountants Ordinance for appointment as auditors of a company\. Such qualified persons include members of the Hong Kong Institute of CPAs \(HKICPA\)\. The accountants must also be independent of the issuer or any other connected company, in a manner acceptable to the HKICPA and the HKEx\.

\(b\) A three\-year history must be provided which must include the disclosures required under the relevant accounting standards adopted \( which can be HKFRS, IFRS, or China Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises \(CASBE\) in the case of a PRC issuer\)\. In addition the three\-year history must disclose separately the following additional information\.

In respect of the statement of profit or loss and other comprehensive income

- Profit \(or loss\) on sale of properties
- Profit \(or loss\) before taxation, including the share of the profit \(or loss\) of associates and joint ventures, with separate disclosure of any items included therein which are exceptional because of size, nature and incidence
- Taxation on profits \(Hong Kong and overseas\) in each case indicating the basis of computation, with separate disclosure of the taxation on share of associated companies’ associates’ and joint ventures’ profits

In respect of the statement of financial position

- An ageing analysis of accounts receivable
- An ageing analysis of accounts payable

In respect of dividends

- Rates of dividend paid or proposed on each class of shares \(with particulars of each such class\) and amounts absorbed thereby
- Details of any special dividend proposed to be paid after the date of the accountants’ report

Any other relevant matters
– There are a number of detailed requirements in respect of pro forma financial information\. The major ones are these:
– The information must state the purpose for which it has been prepared; that it is prepared for illustrative purposes only; and that because of its nature, it may not give a true picture of the issuer's financial position or results\.
– The information must be presented in columnar format showing separately the unadjusted financial information, the pro forma adjustments and the pro forma financial information\.
– The pro forma financial information must be current\.
– The pro forma financial information must be reported on by the auditors or approved reporting accountants\.

# HKEx regulation and reporting requirements

There are a large number of reporting requirements in respect of listing on the HKEx\. There are two major areas that affect CPAs; the accountants' report and pro forma financial information required in relation to listing, and the continuing obligations to provide reports of interest to investors\.

# Corporate governance in Hong Kong \- framework

![](dayone-moment://CA021695A0984CA98C6D2458F6E680EE)

- Both statutory requirements and non\-statutory requirements
- Based on principles
- Non\-statutory requirements \- specified under the Listing Rules of the HKSE, including the Corporate Governance Code

The Listing Rules and CG Code

{"meta":{"version":1},"contents":[{"attributes":{"line":{"header":1}},"text":"Insider dealing
"},{"embeddedObjects":[{"type":"photo","identifier":"EA11DB0FBA3F4288A32D18578F557436"}]},{"text":"
"},{"text":"A category of ‘market misconduct’ under the SFO - Rules: a civil regime and a criminal regime

The Model Code: must not buy or sell shares in the company during particular periods of time

Enforcement:
(a) If a company or an individual is in breach of a law, such as the Securities and Futures Ordinance, a crime is committed. The law can be enforced through the courts, and the company or individual, if found guilty, will be subject to punishment by the court.

(b) If a listed company is in breach of any of the Listing Rules, it has not broken any law. However it (or its officers) may be subject to disciplinary action by the stock exchange (HKSE).

(c) If a company breaches a provision of the Corporate Governance Code, which is a voluntary code, it has not broken a regulation. However if it is a listed company, it is subject to the HKSE Listing Rules. The Listing Rules require companies to comply with the Code or explain any non-compliance. A listed company is therefore in breach of the Listing Rules if it does not comply with the Code provisions and fails to explain the non-compliance.

(d) If a listed company does not follow an item of recommended best practice in the Corporate Governance Code, it has done nothing wrong. The Code suggests that the company should explain in its annual report why it has not followed the recommended best practice, but in contrast to a breach of a code provision, this is not a requirement.
"}]}
entries.text:
# Insider dealing

![](dayone-moment://EA11DB0FBA3F4288A32D18578F557436)

A category of ‘market misconduct’ under the SFO \- Rules: a civil regime and a criminal regime

The Model Code: must not buy or sell shares in the company during particular periods of time

Enforcement:
\(a\) If a company or an individual is in breach of a law, such as the Securities and Futures Ordinance, a crime is committed\. The law can be enforced through the courts, and the company or individual, if found guilty, will be subject to punishment by the court\.

\(b\) If a listed company is in breach of any of the Listing Rules, it has not broken any law\. However it \(or its officers\) may be subject to disciplinary action by the stock exchange \(HKSE\)\.

\(c\) If a company breaches a provision of the Corporate Governance Code, which is a voluntary code, it has not broken a regulation\. However if it is a listed company, it is subject to the HKSE Listing Rules\. The Listing Rules require companies to comply with the Code or explain any non\-compliance\. A listed company is therefore in breach of the Listing Rules if it does not comply with the Code provisions and fails to explain the non\-compliance\.

\(d\) If a listed company does not follow an item of recommended best practice in the Corporate Governance Code, it has done nothing wrong\. The Code suggests that the company should explain in its annual report why it has not followed the recommended best practice, but in contrast to a breach of a code provision, this is not a requirement\.

entries.richText:
{"meta":{"version":1},"contents":[{"attributes":{"line":{"header":1}},"text":"CFA - Code of Conduct - Content
"},{"embeddedObjects":[{"type":"photo","identifier":"5EBD48673DCC4E56820A41715AB54C1E"}]},{"text":"
"},{"text":"The Code covers the following areas:

Conduct of business (paragraph 2) – a corporate finance adviser should ensure that he is fit and proper to conduct his business. This prescribes guidelines and the standard of conduct expected of an adviser in the discharge of his obligation.

Competence (paragraph 3) – a corporate finance adviser should act with competence. He should be honest, of good repute and character, and maintain a high standard of integrity and fair dealing in the conduct of his business, as well as being suitably licensed for the various types of businesses conducted.

Conflicts of interest (paragraph 4) – a corporate finance adviser should avoid engaging in work that is likely to involve conflicts of interest. He should also take all reasonable steps to avoid such situations. An adviser should not unfairly place its interests above those of its clients. Where a conflict of interest cannot be removed, an adviser should decline to act.

Specifically, where the matter concerned relates to the issue of independence of a financial adviser in a transaction involving the Listing Rules, the Takeovers Code or the Code on Share Buy-Backs, such matters should be dealt with in accordance with the respective codes or regulations.

Standard of work (paragraph 5) – a corporate finance adviser should aim to deliver a high standard of work at all times. The Code expects that a corporate finance adviser should act with integrity, due skill, care and diligence in the execution of its duties and responsibilities.

The Code sets out expectations regarding the role and conduct of sponsors in an initial public offering.

Duties to the client (paragraph 6) – a corporate finance adviser should ensure that it acts in the best interests of its client at all times.

Communication with regulators (paragraph 7) – a corporate finance adviser must deal with the regulators in an open and co-operative manner.

Personal account dealings (paragraph 8) – a corporate finance adviser should ensure that all personal account dealings are properly conducted. The Code emphasises that a corporate finance adviser should avoid conflicts of interest when dealing in securities on his own account while discharging his duties to his client.
"}]}
entries.text:
# CFA \- Code of Conduct \- Content

![](dayone-moment://5EBD48673DCC4E56820A41715AB54C1E)

The Code covers the following areas:

Conduct of business \(paragraph 2\) – a corporate finance adviser should ensure that he is fit and proper to conduct his business\. This prescribes guidelines and the standard of conduct expected of an adviser in the discharge of his obligation\.

Competence \(paragraph 3\) – a corporate finance adviser should act with competence\. He should be honest, of good repute and character, and maintain a high standard of integrity and fair dealing in the conduct of his business, as well as being suitably licensed for the various types of businesses conducted\.

Conflicts of interest \(paragraph 4\) – a corporate finance adviser should avoid engaging in work that is likely to involve conflicts of interest\. He should also take all reasonable steps to avoid such situations\. An adviser should not unfairly place its interests above those of its clients\. Where a conflict of interest cannot be removed, an adviser should decline to act\.

Specifically, where the matter concerned relates to the issue of independence of a financial adviser in a transaction involving the Listing Rules, the Takeovers Code or the Code on Share Buy\-Backs, such matters should be dealt with in accordance with the respective codes or regulations\.

Standard of work \(paragraph 5\) – a corporate finance adviser should aim to deliver a high standard of work at all times\. The Code expects that a corporate finance adviser should act with integrity, due skill, care and diligence in the execution of its duties and responsibilities\.

The Code sets out expectations regarding the role and conduct of sponsors in an initial public offering\.

Duties to the client \(paragraph 6\) – a corporate finance adviser should ensure that it acts in the best interests of its client at all times\.

Communication with regulators \(paragraph 7\) – a corporate finance adviser must deal with the regulators in an open and co\-operative manner\.

Personal account dealings \(paragraph 8\) – a corporate finance adviser should ensure that all personal account dealings are properly conducted\. The Code emphasises that a corporate finance adviser should avoid conflicts of interest when dealing in securities on his own account while discharging his duties to his client\.

entries.richText:
{"meta":{"version":1},"contents":[{"attributes":{"line":{"header":1}},"text":"Reasons for listing shares
"},{"embeddedObjects":[{"type":"photo","identifier":"452F37DF64B845DD98E2135CE6A41DF9"}]},{"text":"
"},{"text":"Following advantages:

(a) Access to capital for growth with opportunities to raise funds both at the time of listing and at later stages.

(b) Broader shareholder base could potentially lead to a more liquid market in the trading of the company's shares.

(c) Employee incentive and commitment resulting from the grant of employee share options to tie in the company's key staff.

(d) Higher profile and visibility in the market could generate reassurance among the company's customers and suppliers.

(e) Increased corporate transparency could lead to the grant of credit lines on more competitive terms from the company's bankers.

(f) Greater efficiency resulting from rigorous disclosure standards demanded of listed issuers will lead to an improvement in their control, management information and operating systems.
"}]}
entries.text:
# Reasons for listing shares

![](dayone-moment://452F37DF64B845DD98E2135CE6A41DF9)

Following advantages:

\(a\) Access to capital for growth with opportunities to raise funds both at the time of listing and at later stages\.

\(b\) Broader shareholder base could potentially lead to a more liquid market in the trading of the company's shares\.

\(c\) Employee incentive and commitment resulting from the grant of employee share options to tie in the company's key staff\.

\(d\) Higher profile and visibility in the market could generate reassurance among the company's customers and suppliers\.

\(e\) Increased corporate transparency could lead to the grant of credit lines on more competitive terms from the company's bankers\.

\(f\) Greater efficiency resulting from rigorous disclosure standards demanded of listed issuers will lead to an improvement in their control, management information and operating systems\.

entries.text:
# Applications for Listing

![](dayone-moment://33F95C79DE0F42E397325AD326924D89)

- application made by the company and its advisers to the Listing Committee of the SEHK,

1. Prepare a “listing document”

- if intends to offer the shares for sale —> “prospectus” \(a document that offers securities in a company for sale to investors\)
	- it must comply with the requirements of the Companies \(Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions\) Ordinance, and:
		- Must contain information specified by the Ordinance
		- Must be available in both an English and Chinese language version

2. Listing Division of SEHK checks that the listing document/prospectus complies with the requirements of both

- the Listing Rules and
- the Companies \(Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provision\) Ordinance

3, \.The application is considered by a meeting of the Listing Committee, and if the Committee is satisfied:

- it approves the listing of the company’s shares and also
- Authorize the registration of the prospectus by the Companies Registry

4. Under the ‘dual\-filing’ system the SEHK also provides the SFC with a copy of the prospectus\. The SFC may object to a listing application if the prospectus appears to contain false or misleading information\.

New issues of shares must usually be fully underwritten\. This means that there are investors who have formally agreed to buy any of the shares of the company that are not purchased by other investors\. entries.text:
# Continuing obligations to provide reports of interest to investors

![](dayone-moment://0F91EFE4474C4B729666AA2890838AA7)

Chapter 13 of the Main Board listing rules outlines in considerable detail a set of requirements in relation to the obligation of listed companies to provide reports of interest to investors\. A summary of the major ones follows:

\(a\) The company must inform the SEHK and shareholders as soon as reasonably practical of any matter which:

– Is necessary to appraise the position of the company / group; or
– Is necessary to avoid the establishment of a false market in its securities; or
– Might reasonably be expected materially to affect market activity and the price of its securities\.

\(b\) An issuer must respond promptly to enquiries made by the SEHK concerning unusual movements in the price or trading volume of its listed securities, and issue an announcement where appropriate\.

\(c\) By not later than 30 minutes before the opening of SEHK trading, an issuer must advise the Exchange of any changes in the number of shares, e\.g\. bonus issues, rights issues, etc\.

\(d\) The issuer must submit a monthly return to the SEHK containing such prescribed information as movements in equity securities and debt securities\.

\(e\) Immediately after board meetings the issuer must provide the SEHK with information on:
– Any decision to declare, recommend or pay any dividend or other distribution including the rate and amount of the dividend or distribution and the expected payment date;
– Any decision not to declare, recommend or pay any dividend or other distribution;
– Any preliminary announcement of profits or losses for any year, half year, or other period;
– Any proposed changes in its capital structure; and
– Any decision to change the general character or nature of the business\.

\(f\) The issuer must provide an annual report containing prescribed information and according to a prescribed timetable\.

\(g\) The listed issuer must provide an interim report for the first six months of the financial year\. This report must comply with certain provisions and be issued no later than three months after the end of the interim six months\.

\(h\) The issuer must publish its preliminary annual results as soon as possible after the end of the financial year, and no later than three months after the end of the financial year\.

\(i\) The issuer must publish its preliminary interim results as soon as possible after the end of the six\-month period, and no later than two months after the end of that period

entries.text:
# The process for admission to listing on the Main Board

![](dayone-moment://898159FF302343E1993CCFB14EAA19BF)

1. The company decides to make an application for listing\. This will include an assessment of how much capital it wants to raise from the share issue and how any of its existing shares will be made available for sale to the public\.
2. The company appoints a sponsor \(and reporting accountants and legal advisers\)\.
3. The prospectus is prepared and checked for accuracy and completeness\. It includes an accountant's report and may also include a profit forecast\. Several drafts of the prospectus are prepared until the final version is completed\.
4. Other documentation is prepared, including a formal application for listing\.

An underwriting agreement is prepared and underwriting is negotiated with underwriters\. All documentation and agreements are reviewed and approved by the company’s board of directors\.

5. The application for listing is made to the Listing Committee of the Exchange \(by the sponsor on behalf of the company\)\.
6. The Listing Committee approves the application and the admission of the shares to listing\. It also approves the prospectus, and the company must then file a copy with the Companies Registry\.
7. The prospectus is published, together with application forms for investors to apply to buy shares in the issue\.
8. The applications from investors are processed and shares are allocated to the applicants\.
9. Dealing in the shares begins on the SEHK\.

For a new applicant this process usually takes about six to twelve months

\.

{"meta":{"version":1},"contents":[{"attributes":{"line":{"header":1}},"text":"Minimum requirements for listing on the Main Board / GEM
"},{"embeddedObjects":[{"type":"photo","identifier":"512D376929F64D109965E39D5884B1EB"}]},{"text":"
"},{"text":"New applicants for a Main Board listing must meet several requirements:

(a) In the opinion of the SEHK, the applicant and its business must be suitable for listing. For example, the SEHK will not normally consider a new applicant suitable if it has recently changed the period of its financial year.

(b) The company must (usually) have a trading record of not less than three financial years.

(c) It must (usually) also be able to demonstrate continuity of management for at least the three preceding financial years and continuity of ownership and control for at least the most recent audited financial year.

(d) The company must have a sufficient management presence in Hong Kong. Usually, this means that at least two executive directors of the company should be resident in Hong Kong.

(e) At the time of the expected date for admission to listing, the expected market value of the securities of the company which are held by the public must be at least HK$50,000,000. (At least 25% of the company's total number of issued shares must be held by the public at all times. Not more than 50% of the number of shares held by the public at the time of listing can be beneficially owned by the three largest public shareholders.)

(f) There must be an adequate spread of holders of the securities to be listed. The number will depend on the size and nature of the issue, but in all cases there must be at least 300 shareholders

A new applicant for listing to the Main Board must also pass one of three financial tests:

entries.text:
# Minimum requirements for listing on the Main Board / GEM

![](dayone-moment://512D376929F64D109965E39D5884B1EB)

New applicants for a Main Board listing must meet several requirements:

\(a\) In the opinion of the SEHK, the applicant and its business must be suitable for listing\. For example, the SEHK will not normally consider a new applicant suitable if it has recently changed the period of its financial year\.

\(b\) The company must \(usually\) have a trading record of not less than three financial years\.

\(c\) It must \(usually\) also be able to demonstrate continuity of management for at least the three preceding financial years and continuity of ownership and control for at least the most recent audited financial year\.

\(d\) The company must have a sufficient management presence in Hong Kong\. Usually, this means that at least two executive directors of the company should be resident in Hong Kong\.

\(e\) At the time of the expected date for admission to listing, the expected market value of the securities of the company which are held by the public must be at least HK$50,000,000\. \(At least 25% of the company's total number of issued shares must be held by the public at all times\. Not more than 50% of the number of shares held by the public at the time of listing can be beneficially owned by the three largest public shareholders\.\)

\(f\) There must be an adequate spread of holders of the securities to be listed\. The number will depend on the size and nature of the issue, but in all cases there must be at least 300 shareholders

A new applicant for listing to the Main Board must also pass one of three financial tests:

- A profits test
- A market capitalisation/revenue/cash flow test, or
- A market capitalisation/revenue test\.

# Companies Ordinance

The Hong Kong new Companies Ordinance forms the core of the regulation of companies in Hong Kong\. It sets out the rules and regulations governing Hong Kong companies and the conduct of their affairs\.

A new Companies Ordinance and the subsidiary legislation came into effect on 3 March 2014\. At the same time the core provisions affecting the operation of companies in the previous Companies Ordinance \(Cap\. 32\) were repealed\. However provisions relating to prospectuses, winding\-up, insolvency of companies and disqualification were not repealed and the provisions of the old ordinance \(Cap\. 32\) remain in force on these areas\. Accordingly the old ordinance was retitled as Companies \(Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions\) Ordinance \(Cap\. 32\)\.

- the new companies ordinance applies to all companies formed and registered under Companies Ordinance
- It aims to achieve four main objectives, namely, to enhance corporate governance; ensure better regulation; facilitate business; and modernise the law\.
- The Companies Registry administers and enforces most parts of the Hong Kong new Companies Ordinance\.

entries.text:
# Key provisions of Corporate Governance Code

\(a\) Separation of chairman and CEO – The roles of chairman and chief executive should be separate and should not be performed by the same individual\. The division of responsibilities between the chairman and chief executive should be clearly established and set out in writing\.

\(b\) Board composition – The board should include a balanced composition of executive and non\-executive directors \(including independent non\-executive directors\) so that there is a strong independent element on the board, which can effectively exercise independent judgment\. Non\-executive directors should be of sufficient calibre and number for their views to carry weight\.

\(c\) Remuneration – An issuer should disclose directors' remuneration policy and other remuneration related matters\. The procedure for setting policy on executive directors' remuneration and all directors’ remuneration packages should be formal and transparent\. Remuneration levels should be sufficient to attract and retain directors to run the company successfully, without paying more than necessary\. No director should be involved in deciding his own remuneration\.

\(d\) Internal controls – The board should ensure that the issuer maintains sound and effective internal controls to safeguard shareholders' investment and the issuer's assets\.

entries.text:
# Elements of corporate governance

CG influences the way in which a company deals with its stakeholders\.

- How the board of directors should act in the interests of the company’s stakeholders, particularly its equity shareholders
- The structure and composition of the board of directors: how large should the board be and who should be its directors?

entries.text:
# Companies Ordinance

The Hong Kong new Companies Ordinance forms the core of the regulation of companies in Hong Kong\. It sets out the rules and regulations governing Hong Kong companies and the conduct of their affairs\.

A new Companies Ordinance and the subsidiary legislation came into effect on 3 March 2014\. At the same time the core provisions affecting the operation of companies in the previous Companies Ordinance \(Cap\. 32\) were repealed\. However provisions relating to prospectuses, winding\-up, insolvency of companies and disqualification were not repealed and the provisions of the old ordinance \(Cap\. 32\) remain in force on these areas\. Accordingly the old ordinance was retitled as Companies \(Winding Up and Miscellaneous Provisions\) Ordinance \(Cap\. 32\)\.

- the new companies ordinance applies to all companies formed and registered under Companies Ordinance
- It aims to achieve four main objectives, namely, to enhance corporate governance; ensure better regulation; facilitate business; and modernise the law\.
- The Companies Registry administers and enforces most parts of the Hong Kong new Companies Ordinance\.

entries.text:
# The divisions of the SFC

\(a\) Corporate Finance Division, which is the major division that regulates corporate finance activities

\(b\) Enforcement Division, which conducts market surveillance to identify improper or illegal activities for further investigation

\(c\) Investment Products Division, which uses an authorisation process when dealing with proper disclosure of investment products offered to the Hong Kong public

\(d\) Supervision of Markets Division, which supervises key market operators and ensures that the regulation and the development of Hong Kong's securities and futures markets meet international standards

\(e\) Intermediaries Division comprising the Licensing Department \(which regulates all those required under the law to be licensed\), the Intermediaries Supervision Department \(which supervises licensed corporations and individual licensees on an ongoing basis\)

The SFC has established regulatory committees to which it has delegated some of its functions\. In addition, there are tribunals and panels which are also part of the regulatory mechanism\. The key ones are:

- Market Misconduct Tribunal \(deals with market misconduct, including insider dealing, market rigging, etc\.\)
- Takeovers and Mergers Panel \(reviews takeover rulings\)
- Takeovers Appeals Committee \(reviews disciplinary rulings of the Takeovers and Mergers Panel\)

# Role of the SFC

The SFC maintains and promotes the fairness, efficiency, competitiveness, transparency and orderliness of the securities industry\.

- The SFC has responsibility for supervision of merger and takeover activity involving listed companies\.

Its Corporate Finance Executive deals with any matters referred to it concerning a takeover or merger, or buy\-back of shares by a company, and makes rulings on the matter in accordance with the Codes on Takeovers and Mergers and Share Buy\-Backs\('the Codes'\)\.

entries.text:
## The importance of planning

![](dayone-moment://0EA103B6534D45C7881D81FA3F43E6F5)

```
General term \- HKSA 300 Planning an Audit of Financial Statements
```


**Auditors should undertake the following:**

\(a\) **Plan** the audit to enable it to be carried out in the most effective and efficient manner
\(b\) Consider whether to **continue** the entity relationship in the case of an existing entity
\(c\) Ensure the **terms** of the engagement are understood
\(d\) Consider **ethical** guidance including independence
\(e\) Consider entity **acceptance** procedures and professional clearance
\(f\) Establish the **overall audit strategy** for the audit and update any changes during the course of the audit
\(g\) Develop and document an overall audit strategy for the expected scope and conduct of audit in order to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level
\(h\) Develop and document an ​**audit plan**​ which sets out the nature, extent and timing of planned audit procedures 

The audit strategy and plan should be revised during the audit when there are changes in conditions or unexpected results are obtained\.

Audit procedures should be discussed with the entity's management, staff and/or audit committee in order to co\-ordinate audit work, including that of the internal audit function\. However, all audit procedures remain the responsibility of the external auditors\.

**1\.1\.1 Preliminary engagement activities**

Planning activities establish an **overall audit strategy** for the engagement and develop an **audit plan** in order to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level\.

`HKSA 300`  requires that, at the beginning of the current audit engagement, the auditor must perform the following preliminary engagement activities:

- Perform procedures regarding the continuance of the client relationship and the specific audit engagement \( `HKSA 220` \)
- Evaluate compliance with ethical requirements such as independence \( `HKSA 220` \) 
- Establish an understanding of the terms of the engagement \( `HKSA 210` \)

entries.text:
# Principal obtains control of any of the following

\(a\) A good or another asset from the other party that it then “transfers to the customer”

\(b\) A right to a service to be performed by the other party, which gives the principal the ability to “direct” that party to provide the service to the customer on the principal's behalf

\(c\) A good or service from the other party that it then “combines” with other goods or services in providing the “specified good or service to the customer”

entries.text:
Indicators that seller controls the Goods or services before transfer to the customer \(Principal\) include the following

1. The seller is primarily responsible for fulfilling the promise to provide the specified goods or services, e\.g\. it has the responsibility for the goods or services meeting customer specifications\.
2. The seller has inventory risk before the specified good or service has been transferred to the customer or after transfer of control to the customer\.
3. The seller has discretion in setting prices for the specified goods or services \(although an agent may have some flexibility in setting prices\)\.

entries.text:
# Bill and hold arrangements

customer is billed for a product but it is physically retained by the seller until it's transferred to the customer in the future\.

recognise the revenue \-\-> control has passed, ALL the following criteria:

1. the reason for the bill and hold must be substantive \(e\.g\. requested by the customer\)
2. the product must be identified as belonging to the customer
3. the product must be ready for physical transfer to the customer
4. the entity can not use the product or transfer it to another customer

the seller should consider whether to allocate a proportion of the transaction price to the provision of a "storage service"\.

# Sales with a right of return

![](dayone-moment://988DD9F9DD2A41D388BA44EC3D973A70)

customer can return goods to the seller and receive in exchange a full or partial refund

1. revenue is recognised to the extend that the seller expects to be entitled to it
2. a refund liability is recognised for the consideration received that the seller does not expected to be entitled to; and
3. an asset is recognised for the right to recover products from the customer on settling the refund liability\. Corresponding adjustment is made to cost of sales

- all or some of the goods or services promised in the contracts are a single performance obligation

# Step 1: identify the contract\(s\) with a customer

![](dayone-moment://A8F5529B7A6A464A8C8C488F1D42241A)

"HKFRS 15 is applied"

to a contract with a customer if:

- the contract is approved by the parties to it and they are committed to performing the relevant performance obligations
- the contract has commercial substance
- the parties' rights and payment terms can be identified
- it is probable that the entity will collect the consideration to which it will be entitled \(ability and intention to pay\)

Until recognition as revenue, consideration received is a liability, representing either an entity's obligation to transfer G/S or refund the consideration received

# Disclosure \- revenue

HKFRS 15 requires that an entity provides both qualitative and quantities information about:

\(A\) its contracts with customers;
\(B\) the significant judgments and changes in judgments made in applying HKFRS 15 to those contracts; and
\(C\) any assets recognized from the costs to obtain or fulfill a contract with a customer

# Allocation of discount

Total price for the bundle is less than the sum of individual prices of each of the items included in the bundle —> allocated proportionately to all performance obligations

— Unless there is observable evidence that the discount only relates to certain performance obligation \- ALL the following conditions are met:

- regularly sells each distinct G/S in the contract on a stand\-alone basis’
- Regularly sells on a stand\-alone basis a bundle of some of those distinct G/S at discount
- The discount attributable to each bundle of G/S is substantially the same as the discount in the contract and an analysis of the G/S in each bundle provides observable evidence of the performance obligation to which the entire discount in the contract belongs

# The audit strategy and the audit plan

![](dayone-moment://F4F04F6D78134E4D8DC7A934790EAAC4)

The **audit strategy** sets the scope, timing and direction of the audit, and guides the development of the more detailed audit plan\.

Derived from the audit engagement partner’s understanding of the entity and its particular environment \(HKSA 315 \(revised 2016\)\), which indicate where the most significant risks of misstatements lie\.
## The audit strategy: Matters to consider
**Characteristics of the engagement**

- Relevant financial reporting framework
- Industry regulation
- Expected scope of audit
- Characteristics of business segments
- Existence of an internal audit function and its work
- Use of service organisations
- Effect of information and communications technology on audit procedures
- Availability of entity staff and information

**Reporting objectives, timing of the audit and nature of communications**

- Entity's timescale for reporting and accounting policies
- New accounting standards
- Organisation of meetings with management and those charged with governance
- Discussions with management and those charged with governance
- Expected communications with third parties

**Significant factors, preliminary engagement activities, and knowledge gained on other engagements**

- Determination of materiality 
- Areas identified with higher risks of material misstatement 
- Results of previous audits 
- Need to maintain professional scepticism 
- Evidence of management's commitment to design, implementation and maintain sound internal controls 
- Volume of transactions 
- Significant business developments 
- Significant industry developments and conditions 
- Significant changes in the financial reporting framework 
- Other significant recent developments Any going concern issues

**Nature, timing and extent of resources**

- Selection of engagement team 
- Assignment of work to team members 
- Engagement budget

---

The **audit plan** converts the audit strategy into a more detailed plan and includes the nature, timing and extent of audit procedures to be performed by engagement team members in order to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence to reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level\.

The audit plan shall include the following: \-
\(a\) A description of the nature, timing and extent of planned risk assessment procedures
\(b\) A description of the nature, timing and extent of planned further audit procedures at the assertion level
\(c\) Other planned audit procedures required to be carried out for the engagement to comply with HKSAs 

The planning for these procedures occurs over the course of the audit as the audit plan develops\. 

Any changes made during the audit engagement to the overall audit strategy or audit plan, and the reasons for such changes, shall be included in the audit documentation\.

​**Documentation**​:

- sufficient to demonstrate the planned nature, timing and extent of risk assessment procedures, and further audit procedures at the assertion level for each material class of transaction, account balance, and disclosure in response to the assessed risks\.
- any significant changes to the originally planned overall audit strategy and to the detailed audit plan includes the reasons for the significant changes and the auditor's response to the events, conditions, or results of audit procedures that resulted in such changes\.

entries.text:
# Agreeing the terms of audit engagement

![](dayone-moment://F9FD54423D5A488E8785410328D5FEF1)

In accordance with HKSA 210 the objective of the auditor is to accept or continue an audit engagement only when ​**the basis upon which it is to be performed has been agreed**​, through: 

- Establishing whether the **pre\-conditions** for an audit are present 
- Confirming that there is a **common understanding** between auditor and management or those charged with governance of the **terms of the audit engagement**
## 1\.3\.1 Preconditions for an audit
Preconditions for an audit are the use by management of an acceptable financial reporting framework for preparation of its financial statements and the agreement by management and those charged with governance on which an audit is conducted\.

The auditor must:
\(a\) Determine whether the financial reporting framework to be applied in the preparation of the financial statements is acceptable
\(b\) Obtain the agreement of management that it acknowledges and understands its responsibility:

- For the preparation of financial statements in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework 
- For establishing the internal controls necessary for enabling the preparation of financial statements free from material misstatements 
- For providing the auditor with access to information, any additional information upon request and unrestricted access to persons within the entity for audit evidence
## 1\.3\.2 Agreeing terms with management or those charged with governance
The auditor must agree the terms of the audit engagement with management or those charged with governance\. The agreed terms of the audit engagement include matters such as:
\(a\) The objective and scope of the audit of the financial statements\.
\(b\) The responsibilities of the auditor and management\.
\(c\) Identification of the applicable financial reporting framework for the preparation of the financial statements\.
\(d\) Reference to the expected form and content of any reports to be issued by the auditor and a statement that there may be circumstances in which a report may differ from its expected form and content\. This may be done in an engagement letter or any suitable form of written agreement\.

entries.text:
# Understanding the entity and its environment

![](dayone-moment://B39BB9D09196488D990E61A5DCCC4463)

`HKSA 315 \(Revised 2016\) Identifying and Assessing the Risks of Material Misstatement through Understanding the Entity and its Environment` 

`HKSA 315 \(Revised 2016\)`  states that the ​**objective of the auditor**​ is to identify and assess the risks of material misstatement whether due to fraud or error, at the financial statement and assertion levels, through understanding the entity and its environment, including the entity's internal control, thereby providing a basis for designing and implementing responses to the assessed risks of material misstatement\.

The auditor must perform **risk assessment procedures** to provide a basis for the identification and assessment of the risks of material misstatement at the financial statement and assertion levels\. These must include:

- Inquiries 
- Analytical procedures 
- Observation and inspection

WHY

- To identify and assess the risks of material misstatement in the financial statements whether due to fraud or error other factors 
- To enable the auditor to design and perform further audit procedures 
- To provide a frame of reference for exercising audit judgment, for example, when setting audit materiality and identifying special audit areas 
- To evaluate sufficient and appropriate audit evidence 
- To develop expectations for use when performing analytical procedures

WHAT

- Industry, regulatory and other external factors, including the applicable financial reporting framework 
- Nature of the entity, including operations, ownership and governance, investments, structure and financing 
- Entity's selection and application of accounting policies 
- Objectives and strategies and related business risks that might cause material misstatement in the financial statements 
- Measurement and review of the entity's financial performance 
- Internal control 

HOW

- Inquiries of management the internal audit function and others within the entity 
- Analytical procedures to highlight areas of high risk 
- Observation and inspection of activities and operations of the entity 
- Prior period knowledge 
- Entity acceptance or continuance process 
- Discussion by the engagement team of the susceptibility of the financial statements to material misstatement and the application of the applicable financial reporting framework 
- Information from other engagements undertaken for the entity 
- Reconsider the nature, extent and timeliness of substantive testing

{"meta":{"version":1},"contents":[{"attributes":{"line":{"header":1}},"text":"Impact of the Internal audit function
"},{"embeddedObjects":[{"type":"photo","identifier":"9A6C3515CB354A5C9A07EB58D2941784"}]},{"text":"
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"header":2}},"text":"2.2.1 Risk assessment procedures and related activities
"},{"text":"
"},{"text":"Inquiries of management, the internal audit function and others within the entity

"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"Apart from obtaining information from "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"management"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" and those responsible for financial reporting, the auditor can obtain information through inquiries with the internal audit function, if the entity has such a function, and others within the entity.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"inlineCode":true},"text":"HKSA 260 (Revised) "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"identifies the importance of effective "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"two-way communication"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" in assisting the auditor to obtain information from those charged with governance in this regard.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"Inquiries of "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"employees"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" involved in initiating, processing or recording complex or unusual transactions may help the auditor evaluate the appropriateness of the selection and application of certain accounting policies.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"Inquiries directed towards "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"in-house legal counsel"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" may provide information about litigation, compliance with laws and regulations etc.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"Inquiries of "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"marketing or sales personnel"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" may provide information about changes in the entity's marketing strategies, sales trends or contractual arrangements with customers.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"Inquiries directed to the "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"risk management function"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" (or those performing such roles) may provide information about operational and regulatory risks that may affect financial reporting.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"Inquiries directed to "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"information systems personnel"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" may provide information about system changes, system or control failures, or other information system-related risks.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"As obtaining an understanding of the entity and its environment is a "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"continual, dynamic process"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":", the auditor's inquiries may occur throughout the audit engagement.
"},{"text":"
"},{"embeddedObjects":[{"type":"horizontalRuleLine"}]},{"text":"
"},{"text":"In performing its work, the internal audit function is likely to have:

"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"Obtained insight into the entity's operations and business risks
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"Findings based on its work, such as identified control deficiencies or risks, that may provide valuable input into the auditor's understanding of the entity, the auditor's risk assessments or other aspects of the audit
"},{"text":"
"},{"embeddedObjects":[{"type":"horizontalRuleLine"}]},{"text":"
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"header":2}},"text":"The entity's internal audit function
"},{"text":"
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"If the entity has an internal audit function, "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"obtaining an understanding of that function "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"contributes to the auditor's "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"understanding of the entity and its environment"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":", including "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"internal control"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":", in particular the role that the function plays in the entity's "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"monitoring of internal control over financial reporting"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":". This understanding, together with information obtained from inquiries of management can assist the auditor in identification and assessment of the risks of material misstatement.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"The responsibilities of an internal audit function may include performing procedures and evaluating the results to provide assurance to management and those charged with governance regarding "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"the design and effectiveness of risk management, internal control and governance processes"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":". If so, the internal audit function may play an important role in the entity's monitoring of internal control over financial reporting.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"The auditor's inquiries of appropriate individuals within the internal audit function may help the auditor obtain an "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"understanding of the nature of the internal audit function's responsibilities"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":". If the auditor determines that the function's responsibilities are related to the entity's financial reporting, the auditor may obtain further understanding of the activities performed, or to be performed, by the internal audit function by reviewing the internal audit function's audit plan for the period, if any, and discussing that plan with the appropriate individuals within the function.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"If the nature of the internal audit function's responsibilities and assurance activities are "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"bold":true},"text":"related to the entity's financial reporting"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":", the auditor may also be able to use the work of the internal audit function to modify the nature or timing, or reduce the extent, of audit procedures to be performed directly by the auditor in obtaining audit evidence. Auditors may be more likely to be able to use the work of an entity's internal audit function when it appears, for example, based on experience in previous audits or the auditor's risk assessment procedures, that the entity has an internal audit function that is adequately and appropriately resourced relative to the size of the entity and the nature of its operations, and has a direct reporting relationship to those charged with governance.
"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"If, based on the auditor's preliminary understanding of the internal audit function, the auditor expects to use the work of the internal audit function to modify the nature or timing, or reduce the extent, of audit procedures to be performed,"},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"},"inlineCode":true},"text":"HKSA 610 (Revised 2013) "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":" "},{"attributes":{"line":{"indentLevel":1,"listStyle":"bulleted"}},"text":"applies.
